Description: One tool for tracking how much of everything the company holds: materials, consumables, assets and unique objects. A catalog is configured rather than coded. An administrator builds a unit type out of a quantity dimension and any number of added fields, so a roll of cloth, a stack of miscuts, a laptop and a die are all the same machinery differently configured. Every catalog reports the same four figures - On Order, In-House, Allocated, Available - so a number means the same thing everywhere it appears.

A library is a collection of catalogs and exists for the whole company. What differs per person is which libraries they keep as tabs. Libraries are organised by what things are, not by who uses them, so nothing has to be duplicated to be shared.

Title 3: Switch between libraries with tabs
Description: As a user, I want the libraries I use as tabs above the catalog list, so that moving between them costs one click and I can see at a glance what I have open.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Each library in my view is a tab; the active tab is visually joined to the panel below it.
- Selecting a tab shows that library's catalogs without a page load.
- Which libraries are open and which is active is remembered per user.

Title 3: Take a library off my tabs
Description: As a user, I want to dismiss a library from my own tabs, so that my view stays short.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The x on a tab removes that library from my view only. Nothing is deleted and no other user is affected.
- The last remaining tab cannot be dismissed; its x is disabled and states why.
- A dismissed library is still listed in Add a Library and is one click from returning.

Title 3: Add a library to my tabs from the company list
Description: As a user, I want a panel listing every library in the company, so that I can pull one in without knowing where it lives.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The + on the tab strip opens the panel in the aside with focus in the search field.
- Every library is listed with its catalog count; ones already in my view are marked "In your view".
- An option is a toggle: selecting one not in my view adds it and switches to it; selecting one already in my view removes it. The mark reads "Remove" on hover.
- The panel stays open while I add or remove, so several changes cost one trip.
- The last library in my view cannot be removed here either.
- Arrow keys move from the field into the list and back; Escape closes and returns focus to the +.
- When nothing matches, the panel offers to create a library under the typed name.

Title 3: Rename a library
Description: As an administrator, I want to rename a library, so that it matches what people call it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The pencil beside the library name opens Library Settings in the aside.
- The name is the only setting. Saving updates the tab, the panel title and the breadcrumb above every catalog inside it.
- An empty name is refused with an inline error: a library with no name would be unfindable.
- Cancel, the overlay and Escape all discard without saving.

Title 3: Delete a library
Description: As an administrator, I want deleting a library to say what is lost, so that I do not destroy catalogs by accident.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The trash beside the library name opens a confirmation naming the library and how many catalogs go with it.
- The confirmation states that the action cannot be undone.
- Deleting removes the library and moves the view to another one.
- The last remaining library cannot be deleted; the control is disabled and states why.

Description: An administrator configures what a catalog holds. Two levels of setting: Single-Unit Items belongs to the catalog and is a claim about what a row on its page is; everything in the unit type builder belongs to a unit type and describes how one kind of stock is held.

Title 3: Define a unit type
Description: As an administrator, I want to define a unit type by saying what its stock is counted in, so that a catalog can hold any kind of stock.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A unit type is: a name, what it allocates to, a quantity dimension with its unit of measure and an optional default, and any number of added fields.
- The dimension list is controlled - Length, Width, Height, Count - so the same field means the same thing in every catalog.
- Each dimension offers only its own units: the linear three take in/ft/yd/mm/cm/m; Count takes only "each".
- Changing a dimension pulls its unit of measure onto the new list, so an impossible pairing cannot be saved.
- A default quantity is optional; where it is set, new units of that type start at it.
- A catalog can hold several unit types, each counted differently.

Title 3: Add fields that record what differs between units
Description: As an administrator, I want to record what differs between the units of a single item, so that a roll that is not the standard width is visible.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Add Field adds a dimension, its unit of measure and an optional default.
- A dimension can be used once per unit type: one already taken by the quantity or another field is not offered.
- A new field starts on a dimension the type does not already carry, so the common case takes no edit.
- Each field becomes a column on that unit type's table.
- A field can be removed; its control is always visible rather than hidden behind a hover.
- A field records what varies between units of one item. What varies between items is a catalog property instead.
- With four dimensions, a type can carry a quantity and three fields; Add Field is then spent and states why.

Title 3: Set what a unit type allocates to
Description: As an administrator, I want to say whether a unit type is committed to jobs or to people, so that its table asks the right question.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Allocation is Job or User, set per unit type - rolls go out on jobs, sample boards go out to people, and both can live in one catalog.
- The setting decides that type's column header ("Job Number" or "Allocated to"), its field type and its validation.
- It is presented as two named options, not an on/off switch.
- A single-unit catalog is always User; the control is not shown there.
- Changing what a unit type allocates to releases every allocation of that type: a job number is not a person's name, so the values cannot carry over.
- The panel states how many units the change will release before it happens.
- Nothing is released until the unit type is saved; cancelling leaves the allocations alone.
- Each released unit records the reason in its log.

Title 3: Configure a catalog to hold single-unit items
Description: As an administrator, I want to say that each item in a catalog is one physical object, so that dies and plates are tracked as themselves.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Single-Unit Items is a catalog setting, not a unit type setting: an item cannot be one die and also hold 48 yards of itself.
- When on: the catalog holds exactly one unit type, that type has no quantity and no added fields, its allocation is forced to User, and the catalog has no item page.
- It is locked off while the catalog has more than one unit type, because turning it on would have to discard the others; the reason is given on hover.
- Turning it off restores the quantity and the previous allocation choice.

Title 3: Start a unit type from one built elsewhere
Description: As an administrator, I want unit types saved anywhere in the company offered as presets, so that I am not rebuilding "Rolls" in every cloth catalog.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Saving a unit type files its shape as a preset, keyed by name; saving the same name updates that preset.
- Adding a unit type offers a "Start from" list of every preset.
- Choosing one copies its shape; later edits to the copy never reach back to the preset or to the catalog it came from.
- A preset carries the shape only, never the catalog's Single-Unit setting.

Title 3: Review and remove a catalog's unit types
Description: As an administrator, I want the catalog's unit types listed with what each records, so that I can see the whole configuration without opening it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Each unit type is one read-only row: name, what its quantity is counted in, the fields a unit records, what it allocates to, and a worked example.
- The example uses a field's own default where it has one, so it shows the value a new unit will actually start with.
- Editing opens the builder; clicking the row is a shortcut to the same.
- Deleting asks in place, naming the unit type and how many recorded units go with it.
- The last unit type cannot be deleted; a catalog needs at least one way to hold stock.

Title 3: Leave Catalog Settings without cancelling
Description: As a user, I want a way out of Catalog Settings that is not Cancel, so that reading the settings does not look like abandoning changes.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A back link above the card returns to the catalog.
- The breadcrumb ends on Catalog Settings, with the catalog itself as a link.
- Renaming the catalog updates the back link, the breadcrumb and the browser title as it is typed.
- An emptied name falls back to a neutral label, so the link is never incomplete.

Description: A property is what varies between items - one cloth is Cobalt Blue and another is Copper. Item names are generated from properties rather than typed, so two people cannot name the same thing two ways.

Title 3: Add or edit an item
Description: As a user, I want adding an item and editing one to use the same panel, so that there is one place to learn.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The panel carries every property the catalog has, with this item's value for each. Adding opens it blank.
- Each field matches its property: a vendor is a select, a flag is a switch, a number takes digits only.
- The panel shows the name the item will be saved under, updating as the values that feed it are typed.
- A new item is given the next free identifier rather than being asked for one; it stays editable.
- Cancel, the overlay and Escape discard the draft. Saving updates the heading, breadcrumb, browser title and property chips.
- Which properties exist is a catalog setting; this panel sets their values for one item.

Title 3: Set how item names are generated
Description: As an administrator, I want item names built from a template, so that names stay consistent and searchable.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Catalog Settings defines the naming template as an ordered list of properties.
- The item name is the template's values joined; it is never typed directly.
- Editing a property that feeds the template renames the item on save.
- Properties with no value are skipped, so the name carries no empty separators.

Title 3: See an item's properties at a glance
Description: As a user, I want an item's properties shown on its page, so that I can confirm I have the right item without opening a panel.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Properties with a value are shown as chips under the item name.
- A property with no value shows no chip; an empty property is not a fact about the item.
- The chips and the editor read the same list, so a chip can never state something the editor cannot change.

Description: One row per item, one column per unit type. A user should be able to answer "is this item short of anything" in one look.

Title 3: See every unit type as a column
Description: As a user, I want each unit type as a column on the item list, so that a row tells me the whole state of an item.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Columns are Swatch, Item Name, then one per unit type in the order the catalog defines them.
- Each unit type column shows that type's Available figure; a caption above the table says so.
- Column headers carry the unit of measure, because a catalog can hold a type counted in yards beside one counted in each.
- Adding a unit type adds a column.
- On Order, In-House and Allocated are on the item page, where the units they are summed from live.

Title 3: Spot stock that needs attention
Description: As a user, I want stock that needs attention marked, so that I do not have to compare numbers myself.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A low Available figure is marked amber; an oversold one (Allocated exceeds In-House) is marked red.
- The mark is on the figure, not the whole cell.
- No state relies on colour alone; each carries a tooltip.
- The low threshold is a reorder point, set per unit type and falling back to a catalog default.

Title 3: Sort and search the item list
Description: As a user, I want to sort by any column and search the list, so that I can find an item or rank items by what is short.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Any column sorts; the first click is ascending and clicking again reverses it.
- Blank figures sort to the bottom in both directions; an unknown is not a small number.
- Search matches item name or swatch number and reports how many of the total are showing.
- The list opens unsorted, in the order the catalog is kept in.

Title 3: Open an item from its row
Description: As a user, I want to open an item from its row, so that I can reach its units.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The whole row opens the item page.
- The item name is a real link, so middle-click and open-in-new-tab work.
- Add Item sits above the table, matching every other add affordance in the tool.

Description: The units of one item, per unit type. Fixed columns in every catalog, then one column per added field, so a user who has learned one unit table has learned all of them.

Title 3: Switch between an item's unit types
Description: As a user, I want the item's unit types as tabs, so that I can move between rolls, swatches and miscuts of the same cloth.
Acceptance Criteria:
- One tab per unit type in the catalog.
- Each tab shows that type's rollup, its add action and its units table.
- Columns are Location, Allocated to and Quantity, then one per added field, in the order the unit type defines them.

Title 3: See the four figures for a unit type
Description: As a user, I want On Order, In-House, Allocated and Available for the type I am looking at, so that I know what is free to commit.
Acceptance Criteria:
- On Order is quantity on units with no location: recorded, not yet findable.
- In-House is quantity on units that have a location.
- Allocated is quantity on located units committed to a job or a user.
- Available is In-House minus Allocated and is never stored, so no figure can contradict another.
- Each tile states what it is made of.
- Available carries the low and oversold states, with an icon as well as colour.

Title 3: Edit a unit in the table
Description: As a warehouse user, I want to correct a unit where I am reading it, so that recording a count is not a trip through a form.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Every value in a row is editable in place; there are no save buttons in the table.
- A field commits on blur or Enter and reverts on Escape.
- Focusing a field selects its contents, so typing replaces rather than appends.
- A committed value rebuilds the figures above the table while the table itself stands, so the cursor is never pulled out of a row mid-edit.
- Hovering a row outlines every editable field in it, so the targets are findable from one place.

Title 3: Be told why an entry was refused
Description: As a user, I want an invalid entry rejected clearly, so that I can correct it without guessing.
Acceptance Criteria:
- An invalid entry returns the field to the value it held; nothing is silently accepted.
- A message says what was expected - for example that job numbers are six digits.
- The field flashes an error tint so it is obvious which one refused.
- Clearing a number is not an entry and is not an error; the field returns to its value.
- Emptying an allocation is an instruction - it releases the unit - and is the one blank that commits.

Title 3: Add a unit
Description: As a warehouse user, I want a new unit to start from the type's defaults, so that adding one is a confirmation rather than a transcription.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Add places an empty row at the bottom of the table and puts the cursor in its first field.
- Each field starts at the unit type's default where one is set; fields with no default start empty.
- A new unit with no location reads as On Order until it is placed.

Title 3: Keep depleted units out of the way
Description: As a user, I want depleted units hidden by default, so that the table shows what I can still use.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A unit whose quantity has reached zero is depleted: used up, not an error.
- Depleted units are hidden by default; a Show depleted switch brings them back.
- The table footer states how many units are showing and how many are hidden.
- A unit depleted by an edit dims in place and is only removed once focus has left the row, so a mistyped zero can be corrected without the row vanishing.

Description: For catalogs where the item is the object - dies, press plates. There is nothing within the item to drill into, so the catalog page carries the records and the rollup.

Title 3: Work a catalog of unique objects
Description: As a bindery user, I want a catalog where each row is one physical object, so that dies are tracked as themselves.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Columns are ID, Name, Location and Allocated to. There is no quantity column: a unique record is worth 1 while it exists.
- There is no item page and no drill-in; the item is the unit.
- The four figures are a catalog total: records with no location are On Order, records with a location are In-House, and each person holding one adds to Allocated.
- There is no tab strip, because one unit type is not a choice.
- There is no Show depleted switch, because nothing about a unique record can run down.

Title 3: Edit a unique record in the table
Description: As a bindery user, I want to change where a die is and who has it from the row, so that recording a move takes one edit.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Location and Allocated to are editable in place, with the same commit-on-blur, revert-on-Escape behaviour as the item page.
- Several holders can be recorded, comma separated; each adds one to Allocated.
- A record two people have claimed reads as oversold, which is the intended reading rather than an error state.
- The pencil opens the record's properties; its location and allocation are the fields beside it.

Description: Whether stock is spoken for is a fact recorded against a unit, not something inferred from the name of the shelf it sits on.

Title 3: Commit stock to a job or a person
Description: As a user, I want to record what stock is committed to, so that Available reflects what is genuinely free.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The Allocated to column takes the kind its unit type is set to: a validated job number, or a name.
- Allocating located stock moves it from Available to Allocated immediately.
- Emptying the field releases the unit and is recorded.
- Only located stock counts as allocated, so Available never goes negative over stock that has not arrived.

Description: A quantity is typed over, so the number on screen is the whole of what a unit can say about itself. The log is the account of how it got there.

Title 3: See what has happened to a unit
Description: As a user, I want a unit's history, so that I can answer "where did the other 24 yards go".
Acceptance Criteria:
- Every unit and every unique record carries a log, opened from its row.
- The log records quantities entered, locations scanned, and allocations made and released, with dates.
- It is ordered oldest first and reads as the story of the record; the first event is emphasised.
- It opens in the aside, so the rows the user was looking at do not move.
- It names the record it belongs to, because the panel covers the row that would otherwise say so.
- It is append-only and is never the source of a figure: it says what happened, the unit says what is true now.

Description: Rules that hold everywhere. They are what let someone who has learned one screen use the next one without being taught again.

Title 3: Meet the same four figures everywhere
Description: As a user, I want a figure to mean the same thing on every page, so that I can trust a number without checking where it came from.
Acceptance Criteria:
- On Order, In-House, Allocated and Available are defined once and reported identically for every unit type and every catalog.
- Available is always derived, never stored.
- Every figure states its unit of measure.

Title 3: Do substantial work in the aside
Description: As a user, I want anything larger than a row to open in the same panel, so that I know where to look.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Editing a unit type, adding or editing an item, adding a library, changing library settings and reading an activity log all open in the aside.
- Every aside edits a draft: Cancel, the overlay and Escape discard cleanly.
- What belongs in a table row is edited in the table row.

Title 3: Be told what a deletion takes with it
Description: As a user, I want to be told what a deletion takes with it, so that I do not lose work by accident.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Deleting a library or a unit type names the thing and states what goes with it.
- Deleting the last library or the last unit type is prevented, and the control states why.
- A setting that would have to discard work to be turned on is locked rather than destructive.

Description: The warehouse and bindery already carry handheld scanners. This is the quantity tool on that device: scan a location or unit barcode and act on what came back. It is deliberately narrow - a record enters the app by being scanned and no other way, so every entry is anchored to a label somebody physically read. It records what was used, moves a unit, allocates it and releases it; everything else stays on the desktop.

Title 3: Open a record by scanning its barcode
Description: As a warehouse operator, I want to scan any barcode and land on the right screen, so that I do not have to know what kind of label I just read.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Scanning a unit barcode opens the unit screen; scanning a location barcode opens the location screen.
- The operator is never asked which kind of label it was - the scan resolves to a record and the app routes on it.
- A code that matches no record is rejected with the code repeated back.
- A barcode of the wrong kind for the current screen is rejected by name - "that is a job barcode" - not as "not found".
- No unit, location or job can be opened anywhere in the app except by scanning it. There is no browse and no search.

Title 3: Enter a code by hand when a label will not read
Description: As a warehouse operator, I want to type a code on any screen that expects a scan, so that a rubbed or torn label does not stop the job.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Every screen that accepts a scan also has a text entry with the same effect.
- Enter commits the entry, so a scanner that emits a newline and a person typing follow the same path.
- A rejected entry keeps the field contents, flashes the field and states the reason.

Title 3: See what a scanned unit is and where it stands
Description: As a warehouse operator, I want the unit screen to open with what I am holding and its current state, so that I can confirm I have the right thing before I touch anything.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The header names the unit by Library > Catalog > Unit type, then the item name and the barcode.
- A status pill reads Available, Allocated to <holder>, or On order - no location. The holder is named, never just "allocated".
- The current quantity is the largest figure on the screen, with its unit of measure.
- Location and the unit type's added fields are listed; nothing that is already stated elsewhere on the screen is repeated as a row.
- A single-unit record shows no quantity figure.

Title 3: Record what was used from a unit
Description: As a bindery operator, I want to enter either how much I used or how much is left, so that I can record it whichever way I measured it.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Amount used and New quantity are both editable; filling either one fills the other from the current quantity.
- The field the system filled is visibly marked as derived.
- An amount used greater than the current quantity is refused with the reason, not clamped.
- Save is unavailable until the quantity would actually change.
- Saving writes one history entry naming the before and after quantities and the amount used.

Title 3: Correct a count that is wrong
Description: As a warehouse operator, I want to correct a unit's current quantity, so that a miscount can be fixed on the floor rather than reported to someone else.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Current quantity is read-only until the correction is explicitly chosen, so it cannot be edited by mistake in the normal flow.
- Choosing the correction resets Amount used and New quantity, because the figure underneath them has changed.
- A correction is recorded as a stocktake adjustment, distinct from use, and says so in the history.

Title 3: Move a unit to a new location
Description: As a warehouse operator, I want to scan the shelf a unit is going to, so that putting something away is one scan rather than a form.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The screen states where the unit is now and where it is going; the destination reads Not scanned until one is read.
- Only a location barcode is accepted. Anything else is rejected by name.
- The unit's current location is not offered and is refused if entered.
- Saving removes the unit from its old location, adds it to the new one, and writes a history entry naming both.

Title 3: Allocate a unit to a job or a person
Description: As a bindery operator, I want to commit a unit to the job or person taking it, so that the next person to look for it knows where it went.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The unit type decides whether the screen takes a job or a person. The operator is never offered the choice.
- The screen's title, scan prompt, entry label and rejection all name the one kind it accepts.
- A job number is validated before it is accepted.
- A unit that is already allocated reads Reallocate throughout, and states who currently holds it.
- Saving writes a history entry naming the new holder.

Title 3: Release an allocation
Description: As a bindery operator, I want to release a unit back to available, so that stock returned to the shelf stops reading as committed.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Release is its own action on the unit screen, not an emptied field, and states who currently holds the unit.
- The action is absent when the unit is not allocated.
- Releasing returns the unit to available and writes a history entry.

Title 3: See what a location holds
Description: As a warehouse operator, I want to scan a shelf and see what is on it, so that I can check a location against what the system believes.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The screen names the location and lists the units stored there, each with its unit type, its holder or Available, and its quantity.
- The number of units is shown against the list heading rather than as a separate figure.
- Nothing is derived from the barcode string itself and presented as if it were a property of the location.
- An empty location says so and points at storing something there.
- Rows in the list are not selectable - the list is a record of what is here, not a way into units that have not been scanned.

Title 3: Read the history of a unit or a location
Description: As a warehouse operator, I want to see what has happened to a unit or a location, so that I can settle a discrepancy where I am standing.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A unit's history lists quantities entered, allocations made and released, and moves, oldest first.
- A location's history lists what has come and gone from it.
- The timeline is the same component as the desktop unit history and the job page Scan History.
- The history is read-only.

Title 3: Be warned before leaving unsaved work
Description: As a warehouse operator, I want to be asked before backing out of an entry I have not saved, so that a half-finished count is not lost by a stray tap.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Backing out of Adjust Quantity, Move or Allocate with an unsaved entry asks first.
- The prompt names what would be lost - the quantity, the destination, or the holder - rather than asking generically.
- Keeping editing returns to the screen with the entry intact.
- Discarding clears the entry and leaves.
- Cancel is not guarded: it is labelled, and discarding is what it was chosen to do.

Title 3: Know an action was saved and get to the next one
Description: As a warehouse operator, I want a plain confirmation of what was recorded, so that I can move to the next item without checking.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The confirmation states what changed in the operator's terms - the amount used, the new location, the new holder.
- The primary action is scanning the next label; returning to the unit just acted on is secondary.
- The entry is cleared, so the next visit to the screen starts empty.

Title 3: Skip quantity where a record has none
Description: As a bindery operator scanning a die, I want no quantity controls at all, so that I am not offered an action that cannot apply.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A single-unit record shows no Adjust quantity action and no quantity figure - absent, not disabled.
- Move, allocate and release behave as they do for any other unit.
- Its allocation is to a person, as its unit type requires.
